minutes.headline: Committee ratified the teachers' union MOA and re-voted limits on middle schoolers joining high school teams.
minutes.summary: The School Committee approved the teachers' union MOA unanimously, approved posting a crossing guard and an office clerk position, and re-voted a clarified rule on grade 6-8 students on high school teams. It also heard a teaching and learning update, a warning that the bus contract's fourth-year option looks too costly, the FY23 budget timeline, a resident's request to endorse a pesticide bill, and the FY21 year-end balance report.

public_comment.topic: Chair invited public comment on agenda items; none offered.
Asked the committee to endorse House bill 926 restricting toxic pesticides near schools and child care centers.
Public comment on open items; none came forward.

votes.motion: Approve the Lunenburg Education Association MOA
Accept the two positions (crossing guard and office clerk) to post
Waive the second reading of policies 3201 and 3203.01
No grade six students in tryouts or on a high school team; grade 7 and 8 only to fill a roster; no 7th/8th graders placed if high schoolers are cut

budget_items.what_was_said: Funding for the reinstated crossing guard would come from the transportation budget.
A roughly 10-hour clerk position would be funded by reducing overtime back to its original amount plus the salary difference from a retirement replacement.
The fourth-year option carries a large increase over prior annual increases; the business manager recommended bidding instead.
The FY21 balance came in high, driven by COVID grants covering planned purchases, transportation savings, health insurance surplus and circuit breaker timing.
A DESE grant covers the math learning platform this year; the reading platform is being purchased.

transfers.description: No line item transfers this evening
Last-minute journal entry moving circuit breaker out-of-district tuition expenses to the revolving account, and eligible revolving expenses back to local budget

decisions.decision: Formal vote on the bus contract fourth-year option to come at the next meeting; the business manager will bid the contract around January.
Pesticide bill endorsement to go on the next agenda for a vote, after facilities reports.
The FY23 budget timeline was accepted as tentative and will be shared with the Finance Committee.

what_happened.line: The School Committee unanimously approved the memorandum of agreement with the Lunenburg Education Association.
The committee voted to post two positions, a crossing guard and a part-time office clerk at Turkey Hill; the minutes record the vote as not audible.
The business manager advised against the bus contract's fourth-year option, citing a large increase, and plans to bid the contract around January; a formal vote is due next meeting.
The committee re-voted a clarified rule on grade 6-8 students on high school teams: no grade 6; grades 7 and 8 only to fill a roster.
The FY21 year-end balance was reported high, with COVID grants, transportation savings, health insurance and circuit breaker timing named as drivers.

why_it_matters: The bus contract decision sets what the district pays for student transportation, a line that comes out of the town budget, mostly taxes, and the choice between the option and a re-bid is due next meeting.

The crossing guard is to be funded from the transportation budget and the clerk from reduced overtime and a retirement replacement, so both positions are paid for inside existing school lines rather than by new money.
A high FY21 balance was driven in part by one-time grants and timing, so it says little about what the FY23 budget will need.
watch_next: Formal vote on the bus contract's fourth-year option at the next School Committee meeting.
Pesticide bill H926 endorsement on a coming agenda, after facilities reports.
